limits: The theorem is an implication from five explicit mathematical propositions; the kernels do not prove those inputs or their literature fidelity.
The checks validate the literal Lean definitions and statement, not their equivalence with the intended informal mathematics.
Nanoda is an independent Rust type checker. Comparator replays the exported proof in Lean’s kernel; it is not a third independent kernel.
The positive checkers share Lean’s proof export. Source review, source/object hash guards and canonical Init comparison give additional evidence, not a proof of perfect exporter/compiler correctness.
No hardened adversarial OS sandbox was used. No finite audit guarantees the absence of all kernel, compiler or modeling bugs.
The optional script requires externally built pinned checker binaries, whose hashes are recorded. It does not install them or ship compiler caches/large proof exports.

The focused positivity, recursor and universe controls cover selected rejection paths; they are not a formal proof of the checker implementations or exhaustive tests of universe/inductive combinations.

Kernel conversion rules, proof irrelevance, quotient primitives, and natural-number/string computation remain trusted implementations. Canonical Init comparison protects the definitions those rules expect, but does not prove the algorithms correct.

The publication copy was freshly compiled locally; pinned external caches were reused. The public script independently replayed the resulting main proof, not every unrelated theorem in the public roots.

checker_coverage_review.status: READ-ONLY IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW, NOT A FORMAL VERIFICATION OF EITHER CHECKER

nanoda.classification: Independent Rust external type checker for exported Lean declarations.
nanoda.inductives: Reconstructs the inductive block, checks constructor positivity and universe size, generates recursor types and computation rules, verifies the exact recursor-name set, and compares supplied constructor/recursor metadata with generated data. Nested inductives use specialization and restoration comparisons.
nanoda.universes: Checks universe-parameter uniqueness and scope, substitution arity, sort formation, and max/imax inequalities.
nanoda.conversion: Implements beta/let/recursor/projection reduction, eta and proof irrelevance. Proof irrelevance compares the proposition types; it does not identify proofs of different propositions.
nanoda.primitives: The configured natural-number and string extensions use dedicated computation paths. Their intended definitions are independently compared against a pristine Lean Init export by Comparator.
nanoda.axioms: Nanoda permits axioms by name and checks their types are well formed. The exact allowed axiom types are separately checked by Comparator against pristine Lean Init; a name alone does not certify an intended axiom.

comparator.classification: Statement/definition comparator plus replay into the Lean 4.35.0-rc3 kernel, starting from an empty kernel environment.
comparator.inductives: Lean replay sends inductive specifications and constructors to the kernel, then checks all exported constructor and recursor records equal the generated records; exported recursor rules are not simply trusted.
comparator.quotients: The Quot declaration creates the kernel quotient primitives; Comparator separately checks the exported Quot, Quot.mk, Quot.lift and Quot.ind records against the final kernel environment.
comparator.unsafe: Lean replay skips unsafe/partial declarations. Nanoda rejects unsafe/partial declarations, and the production proof closure was separately scanned for unsafe source declarations and unapproved axioms.

checker_coverage_review.shared_boundary: Both credited main checks consume the same Lean 4.26 proof export. Export completeness and correspondence with intended source semantics are not independently proved by this audit. Tool source pins and supplied binary hashes identify trusted artifacts; they do not establish binary/source correspondence.
